definition: Adjective meaning lustful or lecherous; feeling or openly displaying intense sexual desire toward another.
notes: Standard literary adjective; not confined to sexual contexts (can mean 'craving' generally) but defaults to sexual desire when context is clear.

definition: Adjective meaning voluptuous or sensually lustful; reveling in or characterized by gratification of physical and sensual pleasures.
notes: More elevated register than 'lüstern'; implies delight in sensual indulgence rather than predatory lechery; derived from 'Wollust' (voluptuousness/sensual pleasure).

definition: Adjective meaning lascivious; displaying or expressing sexual desire in an openly provocative or indecent manner.
notes: Direct cognate of English 'lascivious'; appears frequently in journalistic and literary-critical writing about film, performance, or body language.

definition: Adjective meaning eager or desirous; in sexual contexts, intensely wanting sexual contact or gratification.
notes: General German word for eager/craving (e.g. 'begierig auf Essen') that extends naturally to sexual desire; not inherently sexual and carries no crude charge on its own.

definition: Past participle used as adjective meaning sexually aroused or excited; the standard colloquial and semi-clinical term for a state of sexual arousal.
notes: Also used in non-sexual contexts (agitated, emotionally stirred, excited); disambiguated by context. 'Sexuell erregt' is the unambiguous clinical phrasing.

definition: Colloquial adjective meaning turned on or sexually aroused; a dialectal or shortened variant of the standard past-participle form 'aufgegeilt.'
notes: 'Aufgegeil' omits the standard German participial -t ending; functions as a regionally or stylistically marked shortening of 'aufgegeilt'; lower recognition because it deviates from morphological norms.

definition: Past participle used as adjective meaning turned on or horny; crude colloquial slang derived from the separable verb 'aufgeilen' (to arouse/turn on).
notes: Standard morphological form of the participial adjective; crude but widely understood across all German-speaking regions; the most direct colloquial equivalent of English 'horny' when applied to a state rather than a disposition.

definition: Compound adjective meaning sexually frustrated; describing someone who strongly desires sexual activity but is unable to obtain it.
notes: Descriptive compound; not inherently crude but carries the implication of unsatisfied desire verging on desperation. 'Sexual_desperation' is the closest registry concept, though the German phrase lacks the needy/off-putting connotation of that English gloss.

definition: Adjective meaning sexually inhibited or uptight; describing someone who is tense and unable to relax about sexuality due to psychological or cultural constraints.
notes: Literally 'jammed/stuck' (from 'klemmen'); the single most common German colloquial term for sexual and social inhibition; considerably more vivid and widely used than its near-synonym 'gehemmt.'

definition: Adjective meaning prudish; excessively modest or easily shocked by sexual content, language, or behavior.
notes: Direct cognate; borrowed into German from French 'prude.' Mild and neutral in register; used descriptively rather than as an insult in most contexts.

definition: Adjective meaning sexually frigid; lacking sexual responsiveness or desire, historically applied as both a clinical diagnosis and a pejorative almost exclusively to women.
notes: Widely regarded as an outdated and sexist clinical category; the DSM removed 'frigidity' as a diagnosis decades ago, but the term persists in colloquial German as a pejorative for an unresponsive partner.

definition: Adjective meaning sour and prudishly ill-tempered; describes someone who is not merely modest but crotchety and bitterly moralistic about sexuality and propriety.
notes: Stronger and more emotional than 'prüde'; implies that the person's puritanism comes with an actively sour, resentful affect. Etymology uncertain; possibly related to 'verbissen' (dogged/bitter). Somewhat declining in everyday use.

definition: Adjective meaning squeamish, fussy, or overly dainty; in sexual contexts, describes someone who is delicately fastidious or prudishly finicky about explicit topics or acts.
notes: Broader than sexual prudishness alone; the colloquial command 'Sei nicht so zimperlich!' ('don't be such a prude / stop being squeamish') is one of the most common everyday deployments.

definition: Adjective meaning ossified or rigidly set in one's ways; in sexual contexts, describes someone whose attitudes have hardened into inflexible conservatism that resists any liberalizing influence.
notes: Literally 'boned over / calcified'; implies that conservative attitudes are so entrenched they have become structural rather than merely chosen; not exclusively sexual.

definition: Adjective meaning narrow-mindedly bourgeois or conventionally conservative; in sexual contexts, describes someone who disapproves of any behavior deviating from respectable middle-class sexual norms.
notes: From 'Spießbürger' (petty bourgeois, philistine); primarily a social and political descriptor that naturally extends to sexual conservatism without being sexually specific; carries connotations of conformism and fear of social judgment.

definition: Past participle used as adjective meaning thawed out or loosened up; describes someone who has shed their sexual or social inhibitions and become more relaxed and open.
notes: Inverse of 'verklemmt'; maps to the sexual_inhibition concept because that is the governing state being described, even though 'aufgetaut' signals its dissolution. Used approvingly.

definition: Idiom meaning 'hot as deep-fryer fat'; a crude colloquial expression for someone who is extremely sexually aroused or insatiably horny.
notes: Colorful colloquial idiom; the 'greasy, scalding' imagery evokes uncontrolled animalistic heat; more regional and informal than 'aufgegeilt'; not documented in standard dictionaries but circulates widely in spoken and internet German.

definition: Idiom meaning 'hot as coal'; a crude colloquial expression for someone who is intensely sexually aroused or burning with desire.
notes: Less vivid and less widely attested than 'heiß wie Frittenfett'; coal heat is a more traditional metaphor and the expression skews slightly older in usage demographics.

definition: Adjective derived from 'Brunft' (animal rutting season); applied crudely to humans to mean in rut or driven by uncontrolled animalistic sexual urges.
notes: Technically zoological/hunting vocabulary; when applied to humans it is deliberately dehumanizing and crudely comic; the 'ft' consonant cluster makes it phonologically guttural, amplifying its crude register.

definition: Noun meaning rutting season in ungulates (especially deer); applied figuratively and crudely to humans to describe an overpowering animalistic sexual urge or season of heightened desire.
notes: The standard zoological term in hunting and wildlife biology; crude charge arises only when applied to humans. 'Die Brunft' officially refers to male deer; broader uses apply to other ungulates.

definition: Prepositional phrase meaning 'in heat'; used in standard German for animals in estrus and applied crudely to humans to mean overwhelmed by animalistic sexual desire.
notes: 'Brunst' applies more broadly than 'Brunft' (covers females and multiple species); both terms become crude when applied to humans, but 'Brunst' is the more widely applied zoological noun and thus the more familiar humanized insult.

definition: Adjective and noun meaning homosexual; the standard clinical and formal German term for same-sex sexual attraction or identity.
notes: The term 'homosexuell' was coined by Karl-Maria Kertbeny in 1869 in a letter arguing against Paragraph 143 of the Prussian Penal Code; the German word predates and gave rise to the English. Germany criminalized male homosexuality under Paragraph 175 until 1994.

definition: Adjective and noun meaning heterosexual; the standard clinical and formal German term for opposite-sex sexual attraction or identity.
notes: Also coined by Kertbeny in 1868–1869 as a pair-term alongside 'homosexuell'; both entered German medical discourse before entering English.

definition: Adjective and noun meaning bisexual; the standard clinical and formal German term for sexual attraction to more than one gender.
Adjective and noun meaning asexual; the standard term for experiencing little or no sexual attraction to others, used both clinically and as an identity label.
notes: Noticeably lower recognition than 'homosexuell,' 'heterosexuell,' and 'bisexuell' because public awareness of asexuality as a recognized sexual orientation remains limited in German-speaking populations; growing with internet discourse.
